key_insight: RedSage is a cybersecurity-focused generalist LLM built by continual pretraining on 11.8B tokens from 28.6K curated documents, showing that large-scale, domain-targeted data curation produces practical, privacy-conscious assistants for SOC workflows.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between proprietary API assistants (which risk data exposure) and generic open models (which lack cybersecurity domain adaptation) by providing a tuned LLM tailored to diverse security workflows while enabling privacy-preserving deployment.
method: Curate 11.8B tokens via large-scale web filtering plus manual collection of high-quality cybersecurity resources spanning frameworks, offensive techniques, and tools (28.6K docs).
Continual pretraining / domain adaptation of an open base LLM on the curated corpus to produce RedSage with improved cybersecurity knowledge.
Evaluate and design for privacy-safe deployment (on-prem or enterprise-controlled) and benchmark performance on security-relevant tasks.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners and security teams to deploy a domain-adapted LLM that improves accuracy on security tasks, automates analyst workflows, and reduces reliance on external APIs that can leak sensitive data.
visual_elements: Data pipeline diagram: web crawl → filtering → manual curation → 11.8B-token corpus (28.6K docs).
Model workflow: base LLM → continual pretraining → RedSage (icons for domain adaptation).
Before/after bar chart: baseline open model vs RedSage on representative cybersecurity tasks (detection, triage, tooling).
Deployment/privacy icon set: on-prem shield, API vs on-prem comparison infographic.
paper_authors: Naufal Suryanto, Muzammal Naseer, Pengfei Li, Syed Talal Wasim, Jinhui Yi
